logline: A powerless boy inherits the world's greatest hero's Quirk and enrolls in a superhero high school, carrying the weight of a dying legacy against a society on the edge of total collapse.

renewal.note: The eight-season run concluded in December 2025 after Bones animated all 122 manga volumes. A television special adapting bonus manga content aired in May 2026.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 10 critics; strong franchise launch that critics credited with confident tone-setting, though the short episode count limits depth relative to later seasons.

pull_quotes.text: My Hero Academia has most of the qualities people value in a great anime.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 (Spring 2016, Bones) introduces Izuku Midoriya's world of Quirks with the pacing and visual confidence of a studio that already knows its best episodes lie ahead. Critics were unanimous at 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 10 reviews, praising the underdog premise and Bones' kinetic action design. IGN's Alex Osborn gave the first season a 9/10, noting the action and characters while flagging underdeveloped villains - a structural patience the show earns back across later arcs. The 13-episode season is consciously a foundation: it establishes All Might's presence and the UA entrance exam without overextending. The audience IMDb rating of 8.2 reflects solid appreciation for what remains a franchise-defining year for shonen anime.

episode_reviews.title: Izuku Midoriya: Origin
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere announces its thesis in under 25 minutes: a boy with no power watching a world that has decided he cannot be a hero. Bones' animation is restrained here - the spectacle comes later - but the emotional architecture is already in place, and All Might's first transformation is still the season's single best image.
episode_reviews.the_moment: All Might revealing his true form to Midoriya in the alley - the show's first declaration that heroism is not performance.

critic_note.text: An effective start tackling big subject matters in a very unique fashion.

bollymeter.basis: 93% on Rotten Tomatoes from 3 critics; the Sports Festival and Hero Killer arcs are the franchise's creative peak - pacing, animation, and character motivation all in alignment.

pull_quotes.text: Season 2 weaves profound character development into a sports festival with emotionally resonant success.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 (Spring 2017) is the franchise highpoint that most viewers cite first. The Sports Festival arc turns a tournament into a study of ambition and recognition; Stain the Hero Killer reframes the show's ideological stakes from school drama into something closer to genuine moral argument. Anime News Network praised the season's score of 9.5/10 for how it weaved character development into high school structures with unusual emotional depth. Todoroki's backstory episode is the series' most-discussed single hour. The 93% RT score from critics and IMDb's consistent audience tracking confirm this as the season that converted casual viewers into franchise loyalists. Bones' animation hit new highs during the Sports Festival finale.
seasons.season_over_season: Expands the world and stakes dramatically over Season 1's tight origin story; the Sports Festival and Hero Killer arcs are the franchise at full creative velocity.

episode_reviews.title: Shoto Todoroki: Origin
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Sports Festival's semifinal becomes the series' most emotionally charged hour: Todoroki's fractured backstory and his fight with Midoriya function as a single argument about inherited pain and chosen identity. Bones' animation reaches its franchise peak here, and the episode has been cited by critics and fans as the definitive case for My Hero Academia as more than a shonen action series.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Todoroki's left side ignites - the scene the entire season was engineered to deliver.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 9 critics; the Forest Training Camp and Provisional License arcs keep the show's critical approval intact though the expanded cast starts to spread focus.

pull_quotes.text: Gorgeously animated action, an underdog hero and a charismatic cast - My Hero Academia at full speed.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 (Spring 2018) covers the Forest Training Camp villain raid and the Provisional Hero License arc, both of which escalate the League of Villains from nuisance to genuine threat. Critics gave it 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 9 reviews. The Bakugo kidnapping arc is the season's emotional centre, and the All Might vs All For One confrontation is the series' most spectacular set piece to date. Pacing in the license exam arc slows the back half, which is the principal audience complaint visible in episode-level IMDb tracking. Still, the season confirms the franchise's structural ambition and gives Bakugo more dramatic weight than any prior season managed.
seasons.season_over_season: Escalates the villain threat convincingly and delivers the franchise's most spectacular single battle, at the cost of some second-half pacing.

episode_reviews.title: Symbol of Peace
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: All Might versus All For One is the franchise's longest and most expensive single combat, culminating in a status change that permanently alters the show's emotional architecture. The episode's final minutes draw on three seasons of buildup and land with the full weight critics and audiences had been anticipating since Season 1.
episode_reviews.the_moment: All Might's final form and his last words to the watching public - the moment the show had been building toward since its pilot.

bollymeter.basis: The Shie Hassaikai arc is emotionally effective and features Mirio as one of the franchise's finest supporting characters; the Overhaul villain design is divisive but the arc structure is competent.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 (Autumn 2019) adapts the Shie Hassaikai arc, centred on a rescue mission that runs deep into a yakuza operation trafficking Quirk-destroying drugs. The arc introduces Mirio Togata - widely regarded by audience response as the season's standout character - and delivers one of the franchise's most impactful single-episode beats in the Lemillion sequence. Overhaul as a villain received more divided audience response than Stain or Shigaraki, but the emotional stakes around Eri are consistently effective. The Cultural Festival that closes the season provides tonal contrast that divides viewers who preferred the grimmer first half. No formal RT critic aggregation was available for this season at grounding.
seasons.season_over_season: Trades Season 3's war-scale spectacle for a tighter arc structure; Mirio's introduction is the franchise's best new-character work since Todoroki.

bollymeter.basis: The Joint Training arc and My Villain Academia arc are the season's twin poles: the latter is widely considered the franchise's strongest villain-centric writing; the former is routine. Audience IMDb tracking shows Season 5 as the franchise's weakest-rated non-final season.

seasons.review_body: Season 5 (Spring 2021) splits between hero training exercises in the Joint Training arc and the much more critically discussed My Villain Academia arc, which dedicates five full episodes to the League of Villains' origin stories. That villain focus drew near-universal praise from franchise reviewers as the best villain characterization in the series' run - Shigaraki's backstory in particular elevated the antagonist to something with real dramatic weight. The Joint Training arc that precedes it is competent but unexciting. The season ends on the Paranormal Liberation War set-up, which makes it feel transitional despite containing genuinely excellent material.
seasons.season_over_season: The villain arc is the series' best antagonist writing; the surrounding hero-training content makes the season uneven overall.

bollymeter.basis: The Paranormal Liberation War arc is the franchise's most consequential set piece; the season finale became the series-high rated episode on the Japanese review site Filmarks with a 4.4 score.

seasons.review_body: Season 6 (Autumn 2022) covers the Paranormal Liberation War and its fallout - the most structurally ambitious arc in the franchise's run. The first half is pure spectacle: simultaneous multi-front battle sequences that Bones animated at consistent quality across weeks of broadcast. The second half pivots to psychological recovery and societal collapse, trading action for an earned emotional weight. Collider and other outlets reported the Season 6 finale drew series-high ratings in Japan and the highest Filmarks score in the franchise at 4.4. Individual episode IMDb scores in the war arc regularly cleared 9.0. Critics cited this as proof that the franchise had genuine dramatic ambition beyond genre convention.
seasons.season_over_season: The franchise's most consequential single season: irreversible character losses, societal fracturing, and Bones at peak production quality.

episode_reviews.title: The Hellish Todoroki Family, Part 2
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: One of the franchise's most emotionally layered episodes, resolving the Todoroki family arc that began in Season 2 while simultaneously advancing the war-arc consequences. The episode drew the season's highest individual ratings and was cited by multiple reviewers as the franchise's best single character episode.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The confrontation between the Todoroki brothers and their father - the emotional payoff the series had been building since Season 2.

bollymeter.basis: The Final War arc preludes with strong villain-hero standoffs; audience reception tracked positively but the season's split-cour position made it feel incomplete as a standalone arc.

seasons.review_body: Season 7 (Spring 2024) opens the Final War arc, the endgame confrontation between the heroes and All For One's forces that the series had been structuring since Season 5. Bones Film produced this season alongside Bones proper, and the production quality held at franchise standards. Audience tracking showed consistently high episode ratings. The season functions primarily as the first movement of a two-part finale, which limits its standalone verdict - it ends on setups that Season 8 resolves. Screen Rant noted individual Final War arc episodes scored 9.1 or higher on IMDb, suggesting per-episode engagement remained strong even as the season's incomplete arc structure drew some frustration.
seasons.season_over_season: Opens the franchise endgame with Bones' full production resources; works better as a season-7-plus-8 unit than as a standalone arc.

bollymeter.basis: 100% Rotten Tomatoes; Series Graph data shows the final season posted the highest per-episode IMDb ratings in franchise history, surpassing Season 2's peak; Screen Rant reported the finale set a record on IMDB surpassing 2025 competitors.

seasons.review_body: Season 8 (Spring 2025, Bones Film) closed the franchise in December 2025 and was received as one of the year's finest anime finales. Critics gave it 100% on Rotten Tomatoes; Screen Rant reported the finale surpassed a 2025 competitor to set new records on IMDb's episode-level ratings. The season resolves every major character arc from eight seasons - Midoriya's Quirk inheritance, Bakugo's redemption, Shigaraki's tragedy - with the structural patience that only a completed long-runner can afford. Audience reviews praised Bones' decision to commit full production resources to the final battle sequences rather than saving budget. The series ran from 2016 to 2025: nine years, 170 episodes, eight seasons, and one of the defining shonen anime of its decade.
seasons.season_over_season: The franchise culmination: every long-running character arc resolved, Bones at highest production output, and the series ending on audience terms rather than exhaustion.

episode_reviews.title: A Bright Future
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The series finale resolves nine years of accumulated character work without shortcuts or fan-service padding. Bones and Bones Film committed their full production resources to the final battle sequences, and the closing minutes provide the tonal resolution that long-term viewers had been promised since All Might's retirement. Episode-level IMDb tracking placed it among the franchise's highest-rated individual hours.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Midoriya's final moment with All Might - the closing statement on the show's core thesis about what it means to pass on hope.
